messages:
mike: seeing weird throughput wobble on TP all-reduce in the 8-GPU rigs, looks like it correlates with many small KV-cache evictions lately. traces attached in thread.
chao: can you paste the perf-bot alert and the nsys flame? curious if comm stalls line up with kernel selection changes.
perf-bot: alert: tp_allreduce_latency_p95 increased 2.3x over baseline at 2026-03-15T09:12:12Z. top callsites: ncclAllReduce + kernel-launch latency. sample_id=ci-429
mike: perf-bot output. nsys snapshot: https://internal/trace/ci-429
mike: short copy of stack:
```\nGPU0: ncclAllReduce ring (small chunks ~6KB), kernel queue gaps ~150us\nGPU0: launcher selected fused-gemm-kernel-v2 for attention but execution often preempted by comm\n```\n
anya: interesting that ring is still used for those chunks. we should be hitting tree for <32KB in our heuristics, right?
chao: our selector uses msgsize histogram + topology score. but we recently changed the hysteresis so a stream of small fragments can keep us pinned to ring due to windowing.
jen: timeline: regression introduced after batching heuristics change last week? commit 9f3b toggled aggressive microbatching for KV flushes.
mike: yes, 9f3b increased microbatch flush frequency -> more small messages. suspicion: small msgs -> ring path high per-message overhead and worse comm/compute overlap.
chao: can repro locally by toggling kv_flush_frequency to high and running tp 8x4 config. will run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and gather per-chunk timing.
anya: also dump nccl topo and NCCL_ALGO settings. try NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_MIN_CHUNK=16384 to force tree/coalesce.
jen: we should test two fixes: 1) increase coalesce window in runtime so small kv fragments are merged into fewer sends; 2) adjust kernel selector to prefer kernel variants that yield better compute/comm overlap when AllReduce latency high.
mike: quick repro steps I used:
```\nexport NCCL_DEBUG=INFO\nexport NCCL_ALGO=ring\npython perf/runner.py --tp 2 --pp 4 --microbatch 1 --kv-flush 1 --profile nsys\n```\n
chao: running now, attaching initial stats: ring mean allreduce time 420us for 6KB chunks, tree with NCCL_ALGO=tree gives 230us for same workload. overlap score (fraction of compute overlapped by comm) drops from 0.78 -> 0.44 under small-chunk ring pattern.
anya: that's a big delta. suggests our selector/hysteresis is wrong for bursty small-chunk workloads.
jen: low-effort experiment: increase coalesce threshold to 32KB in runtime config and retry.
mike: did that locally: coalesce->32KB reduces number of allreduce calls by ~3x and p95 latency back to baseline. however some microburst latency spikes remain because coalesce introduces small input-tail latency.
chao: tradeoff OK for background generation but might hurt interactive low-latency routes. we need dynamic: route interactive to immediate sends + kernel variant A, route batchy to coalesce.
anya: also saw kernel preemption points in nsys: small allreduce fragmentation causes kernel launch stalls due to CPU driver scheduling; maybe batching on CPU submission side too.
jen: action items:
- chao: profile with NCCL_ALGO=tree vs ring across several msgsize distributions, upload csv (due 3/17)
- mike: add metric for "allreduce_calls_per_request" in trace pipeline (due 3/16)
- anya: prototype adaptive coalesce window (use request tag for interactive vs background) and test perf impact (due 3/20)
- jen: review kernel selector heuristics to bias for overlap-friendly kernels when allreduce latency high (due 3/20)

mike: one more datapoint: on A100 V4 cluster the ring perf is slightly better due to NIC topology, but tree still wins for <16KB messages.
chao: good to note hardware variance. we'll add hardware tag to heuristic inputs.
perf-bot: note: test-run ci-430 completed, p95 reduced after forcing NCCL_ALGO=tree, see job ci-430 link.
anya: ok let's keep root cause: microbatching + kv-flush frequency -> many small allreduce messages -> ring path overhead + kernel launch interaction -> loss of comm/compute overlap. fix = adaptive coalescing + selector tweaks + topology-aware defaults.
mike: sounds good. I'll open RFC with proposed config flags and a short benchmark plan (will include nccl env toggles and nsys artifacts).
